title: Typeform Pricing 2026: Plans, Free Cap and Real Cost
summary: Typeform pricing ranges from $28 to $129 monthly for Basic, Plus, and Business plans. Understand the costs for each tier and what affects your final bill.
body_markdown:
## Finding hidden Typeform costs and limits


Once you're live, three other things change the total, because the monthly price you work out covers only the plan itself:


- the response cap
- the features that are reserved for higher plans
- the seat and renewal terms


Confirm each one on Typeform's pricing page and help center before you pay.


### Response caps and what happens when you reach them


You will most likely hit the response cap first: it's the number of form submissions your plan lets you collect in a month. The cheapest plan is also the one where each response costs the most, so a small tier isn't automatically a cheap one.


If you'll actually use the room, the higher tier is far cheaper per response. That's the point to take from Typeform's chart of the effective cost per 100 responses at each plan's included cap.


Before you launch a campaign, read the help center page on what happens when you reach the cap, because finding out mid-campaign means either responses you can't collect or an upgrade you didn't plan for.


That gap is why you should estimate your response volume first. A tier you outgrow in the first busy month costs more than the one you should have started on.


### Features on a higher tier than you expect


Don't assume a higher plan is the same product with a bigger cap. Typeform reserves some features, such as certain integrations, branding controls and logic options, for higher tiers, and the pricing page lists which plan includes each one.


> A tier you outgrow in the first busy month costs more than the one you should have started on.


Check this list against what you actually need, not against what the form looks like in the demo.


If one needed feature sits two tiers up, that tier is your real price, whatever the entry plan says. Finding that out after you've built the form means rebuilding it or paying more for the same work.


### Typeform seats, add-ons and billing terms


When a plan talks about seats, it means one person with their own login to your account. Plans include a set number, and additional seats are billed on top.


A team that shares a login to save money is breaking the terms, and a team that buys seats pays for each one.


Count the people who will build or review forms, not just the person signing up.


Expect a separate bill for add-ons and connected tools. Anything you attach to move responses into a spreadsheet or customer system may carry its own subscription, so price that connection as part of the total.


If that connection is your extra cost, Activepieces has a Typeform integration that does it as a workflow, without moving you up a Typeform tier.


It is one of 746 integrations counted directly from the[open-source monorepo](https://github.com/activepieces/activepieces/tree/main/packages/pieces/community) , where the Typeform connection has its own directory rather than a line in a marketing figure, so it's a real count.


It is a modest fit: it moves your answers onward and does nothing about Typeform's own price.


If you choose annual billing, the monthly figure drops but you're committed for the year. Check the renewal terms on the pricing page and in the help center, and put the renewal date in your calendar.


If your needs change mid-term, the saving can turn into money spent on a plan that no longer fits.
